original_question: Let p = 2 and G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2). Is the degree-n homology group H_n(G_{2n}; F_2) one-dimensional over F_2 and generated by the determinant class det_n arising from the maximal elementary 2-subgroup A_{n,n}?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Stewart Priddy’s Question 5.2, read together with the immediately preceding setup defining A_{n,n}, the restriction map res, and det_n, and with Question 5.1. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact part of the paper being targeted: p = 2, G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2), the degree-n mod-2 homology group, and the claim that H_n(G_{2n}; F_2) should be F_2 generated by det_n. That is essentially the content of Question 5.2. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
missing_details: The paper asks this for general n, so the quantifier should be made explicit: for each integer n >= 1 (or equivalently, for all n). There is no 'for sufficiently large n' qualifier here. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

A_{n,n} should be defined explicitly as the maximal elementary 2-subgroup A_{n,n} = { [[I_n, X], [0, I_n]] : X in M_n(F_2) }, which is isomorphic to (Z/2)^{n^2}. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

The class det_n is not introduced abstractly; it is defined using H_*(A_{n,n}; F_2) = F_2[x_{i,j} | 1 <= i,j <= n], where the x_{i,j} are the obvious degree-1 generators, and det_n = det(x_{i,j}) lies in degree n. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

To make 'generated by det_n' stand alone, one must spell out the normalizer and restriction map: N_{G_{2n}}(A_{n,n}) = G_n x G_n, so res : H_*(G_{2n}; F_2) -> H_*(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n}. The paper’s shorthand only makes sense relative to this map. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

Because det_n is defined in H_n(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n}, not a priori in H_n(G_{2n}; F_2), a fully self-contained version should say 'generated by a class whose restriction is det_n' rather than literally treating det_n as already a class of H_n(G_{2n}; F_2). This is exactly why Question 5.1 precedes Question 5.2. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

If you want the paper’s motivation reflected, the refined question should note that the degree n is singled out because Maazen had already shown H_i(G_{2n}; F_2) = 0 for 0 < i < n. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
refined_question: For each integer n >= 1, let G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2), let A_{n,n} = { [[I_n, X], [0, I_n]] : X in M_n(F_2) } \cong (Z/2)^{n^2}, and let res : H_*(G_{2n}; F_2) -> H_*(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n} be the restriction map, where N_{G_{2n}}(A_{n,n}) = G_n x G_n and H_*(A_{n,n}; F_2) = F_2[x_{i,j} | 1 <= i,j <= n] with each x_{i,j} in degree 1. If det_n = det(x_{i,j}) in H_n(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n}, is H_n(G_{2n}; F_2) isomorphic to F_2 and generated by a class whose restriction is det_n? ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
justification: The draft is aiming at Question 5.2 rather than merely Question 5.1, because it asks both for the one-dimensionality of H_n(G_{2n}; F_2) and for generation by det_n. The only paper-faithful sharpening needed is to import the notation that the paper leaves implicit in Question 5.2 itself: the explicit subgroup A_{n,n}, its homology algebra, the invariant class det_n, and the restriction map into H_*(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n}. Without that setup, 'generated by det_n' is not literally well-typed, since det_n is first defined on A_{n,n}; the refined version therefore makes explicit that the generator of H_n(G_{2n}; F_2) should restrict to det_n. This stays as close as possible to the paper’s actual intent and does not broaden the problem beyond Section 5. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
